Page store cutover plan

This page walks through moving page state into the Go daemon. It uses every kapi preset, so it doubles as the visual reference for the design system. See the risky step before you start, and the repo for context.

Owner
Track A, the server
Status
in review
Rollback
Flip KAPI_STORE back and restart the daemon.
Note

Nothing here ships until the kapi open command lands on main.

Warning

The cutover drops writes for about 30 seconds. Schedule it outside business hours.

Key point

Go owns all state. The browser keeps nothing and refetches after any reconnect.

Where the state lives

An op from the browser takes this path:

The code

Latency so far

Endpointp50 msp99 msNotes
GET /p/{id}/411Full render with CSS
GET /p/{id}/blocks/{block}13One element
POST /p/{id}/ops619Writes the file and a revision slowest
Why the p99 for ops is high

Every op writes the page file and a revision copy, and both are synced to disk before the reply.

Transport options

Server-sent events

One long GET per tab. Built into every browser and reconnects with Last-Event-ID.

  • No new dependency
  • Plain HTTP, easy to curl

WebSocket

Two-way, but needs its own reconnect and replay logic.

  • Needs a library or hand-rolled framing

Polling

Simplest to build. Adds up to a second of lag and wakes the daemon for nothing.

Steps

Add the page store with revisions under revs/.
Switch the daemon to serve rendered pages and single blocks.
Risk
An agent editing the file mid-request can race a browser op. The store must compare mtimes before it writes.
Delete the old static page handler.
Question
Should undo cross an agent edit, or stop at it?
